notes.about: Kannada, in a script the engine has no rules of its own for: this file is all it knows. Sources: data/manifests/knwiki.json, knwikisource.json, knwikiquote.json, aksharantar-kan.json.
notes.notWord: The digits ೦-೯ and the siddham sign (U+0C84).
notes.firstLetter: Independent vowels, consonants, the nakaara pollu ೝ, the old letter ೞ, and ೠ ೡ. Never a sign, the anusvara (ಂ), candrabindu or visarga.
notes.signs: Vowel signs, the length marks and the virama must follow a consonant. ಂ ಁ ಃ are left out: they can follow an independent vowel (ಅಂ, ಅಃ).
notes.joiners: Not set, so every ZWJ and ZWNJ is dropped, as the engine's default normal form does (and the pack needs no engine 6). Unlike Telugu's, Kannada's text writes the same words every way: of the 9,380 words with at least 50 tokens that ever have a joiner after a virama, 9,357 are also written another way (ZWNJ, ZWJ or none) and 8,457 are written without one most often (ಫುಟ್ಬಾಲ್ 1,298 times, ಫುಟ್‌ಬಾಲ್ 481; ವಾಷಿಂಗ್ಟನ್ 1,170, ವಾಷಿಂಗ್‍ಟನ್ 123). Kept, they would split each word three ways, and a word typed without one would miss the stored form with it.
notes.replace: Two mis-encodings common in the dumps are mended where a letter comes before them. A consonant + Latin ø is the vocalic r sign ೃ from an old font's conversion (ಸಂಸ್ಕøತ for ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತ: about 11,000 tokens, which led the dropped words). The digit zero ೦ after a letter or vowel sign is the anusvara ಂ, which looks the same (ಒ೦ದು for ಒಂದು: about 75,000 tokens); after a digit it stays a digit. The two-part vowel signs (ೆ + ೕ, ೆ + ೖ, ೆ + ೂ, ೊ + ೕ) are ೇ ೈ ೊ ೋ by NFC, which the normal form already applies.
notes.phraseBreaks: Kannada ends sentences with Latin punctuation; the dandas are listed for verse.
